headline: High: caveman’s MCP/file-writing content workflow can feed pipecat’s shared-bus, networked voice stack, creating prompt-injection and data-leakage paths by default.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: caveman can use MCP and writes/reads project files like CLAUDE.md, while pipecat has shared-bus session state and stdin/stdout plus many LLM/STT/TTS integrations. That creates a plausible bridge where caveman-authored content can be consumed as instructions by pipecat, though the exact parser path is not documented. Uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF caveman content is routed into pipecat prompts or tool messages without provenance tags, injection is possible.
IF pipecat treats shared-bus text as trusted instructions, attacker-controlled text can steer downstream behavior.
mitigations: Add provenance labels to all caveman-generated text before passing it onward.
Insert a 1-step human review for any text that becomes a pipecat instruction.
Restrict pipecat to a read-only prompt template for caveman outputs.
Disable shared-bus handoff for untrusted text channels.
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction/data separation in the orchestrator.

B_data_leakage.rationale: caveman touches session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md; pipecat touches conversation state, audio/video/images/text, and can call multiple third-party APIs. In a shared workspace or bus, sensitive text from caveman can flow into pipecat outputs or external services. The pairwise leakage path is plausible in default docs, but not directly proven.
conditions: IF caveman project notes or memory files are routed into pipecat inputs, sensitive text can leave the local workspace.
IF pipecat is configured with any external STT/LLM/TTS provider, shared conversation state may be transmitted off-box.
mitigations: Keep caveman files in a separate directory from pipecat inputs.
Remove secrets and tokens from project notes before handoff.
Use local-only pipecat providers for all speech and LLM steps.
Turn off analytics/telemetry integrations in pipecat.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention filters at the bus boundary.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: caveman supports multiple instances and file-oriented workflows, while pipecat explicitly shares session state across instances on a shared bus. That overlap can create write/write or state clobbering if both agents mutate the same workspace or bus-backed resource. The profiles do not prove a lock, so the conflict remains plausible and nontrivial.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same project files, last-writer-wins conflicts can occur.
IF both agents publish mutable state to the same shared bus, session state can be overwritten or interleaved.
mitigations: Assign separate working directories per agent.
Serialize writes through a single coordinator process.
Disable concurrent edits to CLAUDE.md and notes files.
Use per-session namespaces on the shared bus.
requires-engineering: add file and bus locking with conflict detection.

D_cascading_error.rationale: caveman is a content-writing agent that can emit project notes and instructions, and pipecat is a real-time voice/chat framework with many downstream service integrations. If pipecat treats caveman output as authoritative, errors or fabricated facts can cascade into spoken responses or external API actions. Because the downstream blast radius can be user-visible and irreversible, high is warranted.
conditions: IF pipecat uses caveman output as prompt context without verification, hallucinations can propagate.
IF pipecat triggers external services based on caveman-generated text, incorrect actions can be executed.
mitigations: Require a verification step before pipecat consumes caveman output.
Mark caveman output as draft-only in the handoff format.
Limit pipecat to read-only rendering of caveman text.
Add a confidence threshold before any downstream action.
requires-engineering: implement source attribution and fact-checking gates.

E_compliance.rationale: caveman handles session logs, memory files, project notes, and CLAUDE.md, while pipecat handles audio, video, images, text, and analytics/metrics with allowlisted egress. If regulated or personal data enters the pair, the differing retention and telemetry surfaces can create a compliance mismatch. The profiles do not specify residency or certifications, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than high.
conditions: IF regulated personal data is placed into caveman notes and then processed by pipecat, retention and telemetry obligations may diverge.
IF pipecat sends text or audio to external providers, a policy mismatch can occur.
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in caveman notes.
Disable pipecat telemetry and analytics integrations.
Use providers with matching retention terms only.
Document a data-flow map for the pair.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention policy enforcement.
